subject: Post-call: stress scenario playbook & acceptance matrix
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@orchardai.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orchardai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: stress scenario playbook & acceptance matrix

Thanks again for the call earlier — great alignment. Below is a concise post-call recap and a proposed playbook for the spike/stress run we discussed. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

High-level objective:
- Validate OrchardAI's latency and quality SLOs under realistic production burst and steady-state patterns and confirm the POC success criteria before the pilot ramp.

Traffic & workload profile (agreed on call):
- Steady-state: 8 requests/sec (RPS) sustained for 30+ minutes.
- Concurrent connections: 40 active client connections typically during steady windows.
- Typical prompt length: 50-80 tokens.
- Typical completion length: 300-500 tokens.
- Burst pattern(s): short spikes to 120 RPS for ~2 minutes observed during peak events; also intermittent micro-bursts: 30s at 60 RPS.
- 95th-percentile latency target: <= 300ms end-to-end for text-generation happy path (excluding client-side overhead).
- Acceptable error rate: <0.5% request failures; any sustained increase triggers escalation.

Success matrix (pass/fail criteria):
- Functional: all request types complete with correct structured outputs for 95% of sampled prompts.
- Latency: p95 real-user latency <= 300ms across steady-state and p95 during burst <= 800ms.
- Stability: no node crashes; KV cache growth must not exceed memory threshold in 2-hour run.
- Cost signal: per-token/throughput metrics captured to estimate projected monthly spend at 1M monthly queries.

Runbook (sequence):
1) Baseline run (warm-up): 15 minutes at 6 RPS to populate caches. Owner: Karthik.
2) Steady window: 30 minutes at 8 RPS. Collect perf counters, batch sizes, and cache hit rates. Owner: Ben.
3) Micro-bursts: 3 repetitions of 30s at 60 RPS spaced across 10 minutes. Monitor tail latencies. Owner: Ben.
4) Full spike: 2 minutes at 120 RPS then back to steady. Validate error rate and autoscale behavior. Owner: Karthik.
5) Recovery & verification: 20 minutes steady after spike to ensure no memory leaks and to sample outputs for quality checks. Owner: Team (see owners above).

Instrumentation checklist (we attached a starter):
- Request id tracing (client -> gateway -> runtime)
- Per-request token counts and per-token timing
- Batch sizes and batching latency breakdown
- KV cache hit/miss logs and sizes
- Model variant and quantization flags per request

Proposed schedule:
- Dry run (internal): Tue 2027-06-22 09:00 PT
- Customer-observed pilot: Fri 2027-06-25 10:00 PT

Next steps / asks for OrchardAI:
- Share a 48hr sample of production traffic (anonymized) to help us synthesize replay workloads.
- Confirm a contact who can perform test injections and be present during the pilot.

Attachments: orchard-stress-playbook.xlsx (run matrix + CSV scenarios); redwood-instrumentation-checklist.md

If that looks good I’ll lock the pilot windows and Ben/Karthik will send the load harness and preflight checks.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@orchardai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orchardai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: stress scenario playbook & acceptance matrix

Thanks Vivek — this is really helpful and matches our notes. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we lock dates:

1) Cold start behavior: during the warm-up, do you recommend keeping a synthetic prefix cache population step for the multi-turn flows we use? Our average multi-turn context is ~6 turns which affects KV sizing.
2) Observability: can we stream the per-request traces into our Datadog account (we have a paid integration) or do you prefer we pull logs from a temporary S3 dump?

We’ll pull together an anonymized 48-hour sample and share a link by EOD tomorrow. Tom will be the on-call for the pilot day.

Thanks,
Ellen
Director of Product
OrchardAI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@orchardai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: stress scenario playbook & acceptance matrix

Great questions. Short answers and operational notes: 

1) Cold start / cache priming: yes — we recommend a short "prefix-priming" step during the warm-up that replays representative multi-turn prefixes to pre-populate KV caches. For 6-turn contexts we expect KV to stabilize after ~10-15 warm-up sequences. I added a priming sub-step to the warm-up in the attached spreadsheet.

2) Tracing / exports: we can stream lightweight traces to Datadog (span + trace id only) if you provide a temporary API key. For heavier per-token logs we'd prefer S3 export to keep network overhead off the critical path. Either is fine — Datadog for real-time dashboards during the run, S3 for post-run forensic analysis.

Operational caveats: 
- Autoscaling: Redwood Dedicated will add burst capacity up to configured limits; please confirm whether you want the trial to exercise burst beyond your committed cap (that will incur overage).
- Token distribution: if you can provide token histograms it will let us tune batching thresholds; otherwise we’ll use sampled quantiles from the 48hr dump.

I’ll provision the load harness and send the preflight checklist by Tue morning.

Ben
Principal SWE, Performance
Redwood Inference
